title: Infra GPU Fleet, Cloud Accounts & IaC CI/CD Runbook - Capacity & Networking (2026 addendum)
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary
This addendum consolidates operational guidance for GPU fleet capacity, cloud account topology and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD build/deploy pipelines. It is intended for infra engineers on-call for GPU capacity, platform engineering, and SREs who operate Redwood's inference fleet.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide a single, actionable runbook for capacity decisions, networking changes, IaC workflows, and emergency scaling for the GPU fleet.
- Scope: Applies to hosted inference clusters (prod, staging), Dedicated pools, and customer-private overlay networks managed by Redwood. Does NOT cover model-serving application-level debugging (see eng-serving-runtime docs).

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: infra-platform (on-call rotation).
- Escalation: infra-sre (pager) -> Platform Lead (Marisol Hernandez) -> VP Eng if >2 hours impact.
- Slack channels: #infra-gpu, #infra-deploys, #incident-escalation.

Key services and repositories
- gpu-provisioner (repo: github.com/redwood/gpu-provisioner) - manages instance pools and autoscaling daemons.
- infra-terraform (repo: github.com/redwood/infra-terraform) - central Terraform modules for VPCs, subnets, routing, IAM, and GPU nodegroups.
- ci-cd-infra (repo: github.com/redwood/ci-cd-infra) - pipeline definitions, build images, and release workflows (GitHub Actions + internal runner).
- network-ops (internal service) - BGP/peering and cross-account routing control plane.

SLOs and operational thresholds
- GPU fleet availability SLO: 99.9% across prod region zones (measured per-region monthly).
- Queuing/Provision latency target: 95th-percentile node provisioning < 5 minutes for warm pools; 95th-percentile < 12 minutes for cold scale-ups.
- Queue length alert threshold: queue_depth > 400 pending inference workers for 5 minutes.
- Cost guardrail alert: per-region hourly GPU spend > 120% of forecasted burn for 30 minutes.

Capacity planning guidance
1) Forecasting cadence
   - Weekly: 1-week lookahead for burst windows (sales demos, planned launches).
   - Monthly: capacity reforecast against usage trends and model mix changes.
2) Safety buffers
   - Maintain minimum warm pool of 10% of steady-state pods (min 20 GPUs per prod region).
   - Reserve cold-start burst capacity: extra 5% of monthly peak as spot-backed instances.
3) Adding capacity (summary steps)
   1. Open an Infra Capacity Request ticket (internal template).
   2. Update infra-terraform variables: gpu_desired_capacity_{region}=N.
   3. Run terraform plan against the infra-terraform workspace (see IaC section).
   4. Apply during maintenance window or after approval.
   5. Validate with provisioner_status and test inference jobs.

Terraform / IaC modules & workflow
- Module layout (infra-terraform):
  - modules/vpc (VPC, subnets, route tables)
  - modules/gpu-nodegroup (ASG/EKS nodegroup, instance_types, taints)
  - modules/iam (service roles, cross-account roles)
  - modules/network-peering (peers, route propagation)
- Workspaces: one workspace per account/environment: prod-us-west-2, prod-eu-west-1, staging.
- Secrets: Terraform state in S3 (prod) with DynamoDB lock; remote state access controlled via IAM roles.
- Recommended commands:
  - terraform workspace select prod-us-west-2
  - terraform plan -var-file=prod-us-west-2.tfvars
  - terraform apply -auto-approve plan.out
- PR process: All changes to infra-terraform require a runbook section in the PR describing rollout, canary regions, and rollback steps. Two approvers required (module owner + security reviewer).

CI/CD pipelines and build
- Pipeline roles:
  - build (CI): lint, unit tests, module integration tests (terraform-compliance), image build for provisioner.
  - deploy (CD): staged apply to staging, canary apply to one prod region, full rollout after 30-minute monitoring.
- Canary policy: Apply to prod-us-west-2-c and observe these metrics for 30 minutes: node registration success, provisioning latency, GPU-utilization < 70%.
- Example GitHub Actions job (snippet):
  - name: Terraform Plan
    uses: hashicorp/terraform-github-actions@v1
    with:
      tf_actions_working_dir: ./terraform/environments/prod-us-west-2
- Secrets and credentials: use OIDC for short-lived credentials to cloud accounts; no long-lived static credentials in runner.

Cloud accounts and networking topology
- Accounts: central-org-root -> billing account -> infra (prod/staging) accounts -> workload accounts.
- VPC design:
  - One VPC per region per environment.
  - Private subnets for GPU nodegroups, public subnets for bastions and NAT gateways.
  - Route tables segregated: control-plane routing vs. customer-facing egress.
- Peering and transit: use Transit Gateway for cross-account connectivity; route tables must be updated via network-ops change control.
- Security groups and NACLs:
  - SGs: minimal rules; only control-plane and monitoring ports open.
  - Node SG: egress only to model-store S3 endpoints and control-plane services.

Runbooks: common procedures
- Incident: sudden queue growth (example: queue_depth > 400)
  1. Pager triggers alert to on-call.
  2. Triage: check provisioner logs (kubectl -n infra logs deploy/gpu-provisioner) and cloud console instance lifecycle.
  3. If warm pool depleted, scale warm pool manually: kubectl patch cm gpu-warmpool --type merge -p '{"data":{"desired":"<new>"}}' or update ASG desired capacity in console.
  4. If Terraform drift detected, run terraform plan to detect changes and reconcile manually.
  5. If widespread provisioning failures, roll back recent infra-terraform apply in the canary region and open incident for deployment rollback.

- Incident: inter-region VPC routing break
  1. Check Transit Gateway attachments: aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters...
  2. Re-announce routes via network-ops script: ./network-ops/reannounce-routes.sh --account prod-us-west-2
  3. If failure persists, bring up emergency peering between affected accounts and update route tables with manual entries.

Maintenance & rolling upgrades
- Maintenance window: Sat 02:00-06:00 UTC for non-critical infra changes. Critical security fixes can be applied outside window with 2-hour pre-notice.
- Rolling upgrade policy for nodegroups:
  - Max surge: 10% nodes. Max unavailable: 5% nodes.
  - Monitor: node readiness and model-serving latency per-canary.

Validation and post-change checklist (required in PRs)
- Perf smoke tests: run benchmark/gpu-smoke.sh against canary region and record results.
- Health checks: control-plane heartbeats, node-registration rate, kubelet logs.
- Cost guardrail validation: compare expected hourly spend to forecast after change.
- Post-change: update runbook entry with change details and tags.

Rollback guidance
- For Terraform-induced regressions, perform terraform state rollback by restoring state from S3 snapshot and re-applying the previous plan (document plan id in PR).
- For provisioner regressions, revert docker image tag in ci-cd-infra and redeploy to canary, then full rollout.

Testing & staging
- Staging mirrors prod env (smaller scale) - always run full terraform apply in staging and smoke test before prod PR.
- Use synthetic workload generator (repo: infra-loadgen) to validate autoscaling and warming behavior.

Post-incident review and continuous improvement
- Every significant incident (impact > 30 minutes or severity P1) requires a short blameless postmortem with action items and owner. Postmortems must be linked from the related_pages field and assigned a follow-up tag.

Appendix: useful commands and checks
- Check pool status: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=gpu-provisioner
- Check ASG desired/actual: aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names <name>
- Terraform remote state check: aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-terraform-state --key prod-us-west-2/terraform.tfstate
- Rebuild provisioner image locally: make -C provisioner image-build && docker push ghcr.io/redwood/gpu-provisioner:canary

References
- See also: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026 and /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026
